groups.title: Hazardous-material transportation: recognition and safe handoff
groups.role: Shipping coordinators; Assigned transport document reviewers; Loading supervisors
practicalAssessmentRequired: 49 CFR 172.702(d), 172.704(a), (d) — Hazmat employees performing functions covered by the Hazardous Materials Regulations: Provide the applicable function-specific training and testing and retain the employer training record specified in (d). No universal separate practical examination or VNDRLY evidence upload is prescribed by these provisions. Source: https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/training/hazmat/training-requirements-industry
groups.scopeConfirmation: Actual cargo classification, function and jurisdiction determine applicability; ordinary transport is not automatically regulated hazmat work.

groups.title: Hazardous waste and spill-response role limits
groups.role: Waste-service coordinators; Site supervisors; Emergency planning support; Contractor work-packet reviewers
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.132(f)(2), (g) — Employees using the eye/face, head, foot, hand or personal fall protection covered by paragraph (g): Before that work, demonstrate understanding of the PPE training and ability to use the PPE properly. This is not a separate independent certification requirement. Respirators and electrical protective equipment follow their own standards rather than paragraph (f). Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.132

29 CFR 1910.134(e), (f), (k)(1) — Required respirator users; tight-fitting facepieces require the applicable fit test: Complete the required medical evaluation before fit testing or use, the applicable fit test, and training that enables demonstration of the listed knowledge and respirator-use skills. These duties apply to the actual respirator assignment, not everyone taking awareness training. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.134

29 CFR 1910.120(e)(3), (e)(4), (q)(6) — Workers whose actual hazardous-waste or emergency-response duties fall within the cited provisions: Apply the training and supervised field-experience or response-role competence requirements specified for that actual assignment. Do not assign the hazardous-waste field-experience requirement to ordinary waste handling or awareness-only roles. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.120
groups.scopeConfirmation: Routine waste handling, incidental cleanup and hazardous-substance emergency response are different scopes; do not apply one qualification to all.

groups.title: Process safety and operating-procedure competence
groups.role: Process operators in preparation for plant instruction; Maintenance/operations coordinators; Shift handover personnel
groups.scopeConfirmation: Determine whether the actual process is covered by a process-safety regime; LPG, bitumen, water and utility tasks retain their distinct methods.

groups.title: Bloodborne pathogens and occupational exposure controls
groups.role: Assigned first-aid support workers; Housekeeping and laundry personnel with anticipated exposure; Supervisors coordinating exposure follow-up
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.132(f)(2), (g) — Employees using the eye/face, head, foot, hand or personal fall protection covered by paragraph (g): Before that work, demonstrate understanding of the PPE training and ability to use the PPE properly. This is not a separate independent certification requirement. Respirators and electrical protective equipment follow their own standards rather than paragraph (f). Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.132

29 CFR 1910.134(e), (f), (k)(1) — Required respirator users; tight-fitting facepieces require the applicable fit test: Complete the required medical evaluation before fit testing or use, the applicable fit test, and training that enables demonstration of the listed knowledge and respirator-use skills. These duties apply to the actual respirator assignment, not everyone taking awareness training. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.134
groups.scopeConfirmation: Anticipated occupational blood/OPIM exposure determines applicability; funeral, medical, laundry and care job labels do not establish identical exposure.

groups.title: Food hygiene, allergens and catering controls
groups.role: Camp food handlers; Catering shift leads; Meal transport and receiving personnel
groups.scopeConfirmation: Accommodation, office support and property leasing do not automatically include food preparation or food-manager duties.

groups.title: Laboratory chemical hygiene and analytical task safety
groups.role: Assigned laboratory sample receivers; Analytical technicians preparing for method instruction; Laboratory supervisors and result reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Confirm laboratory-use coverage and actual method; desk interpretation is not bench work, and a laboratory qualification is not clinical licensing.

groups.title: Commercial diving and subsea team qualification
groups.role: Dive-project support coordinators; Client operations contacts; Assigned surface support personnel preparing for qualified instruction
groups.scopeConfirmation: Combined Diving/ROV labels retain unresolved method. Confirm actual human diving versus ROV/submersible work before assigning diver requirements.

groups.title: UAS flight safety and remote-pilot authorization
groups.role: UAS project coordinators; Assigned visual observers and site support; Remote pilots supplementing aircraft-specific instruction
groups.scopeConfirmation: Photogrammetry or media work can be ground-based. Activate flight requirements only for actual UAS duties.

groups.title: Railway roadway-worker and on-track protection
groups.role: Contractor roadway workers preparing for host-railroad instruction; Site coordinators; Assigned rail support personnel
groups.scopeConfirmation: Track workers, passenger train crew, freight brokers and passengers are distinct roles; jurisdiction and contract determine coverage.

groups.title: Industrial radiography and radiation-role authorization
groups.role: Radiation-work site coordinators; Adjacent-trade supervisors; Assigned support personnel preparing for licensed-program instruction
practicalAssessmentRequired: 10 CFR 34.43(b)(4), (c)(3), (f) — Radiographers and radiographer assistants using licensed material in covered NRC industrial-radiography operations: The licensee must provide the applicable hardware practical examination and maintain the required training/examination records. These are radiography-role duties, not requirements for every NDT method or an awareness-course learner. Source: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title10-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title10-vol1-sec34-43.pdf
groups.scopeConfirmation: Keep industrial radiography, well logging, decontamination and nuclear waste as separate qualification subscopes; nonradioactive NDT/logging does not activate source-handling requirements.

groups.title: Electric power qualified-worker task competence
groups.role: Power-work support coordinators; Employees preparing for task-specific power instruction; Host/contractor supervisors
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.269(a)(2)(viii) — Employees doing covered electric-power generation, transmission or distribution work: Demonstrate proficiency in the applicable work practices before the training required by this paragraph is treated as complete. This does not impose the power-industry rule on every employee taking electrical awareness. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.269
groups.scopeConfirmation: Preserve this initial topic separately from TG18 general electrical work. Determine the applicable electrical regime rather than treating all electrical services as electric-power work.

groups.title: Marine vessel duties, transfer and survival competence
groups.role: Visiting marine contractors and surveyors; Vessel/shore project coordinators; Personnel preparing for actual deck/support instruction
groups.scopeConfirmation: Marine consultants, surveyors, passengers, deck crew and masters have different duties. Diving and engineered floatover/lifting remain additional specialist subscopes.

groups.title: Explosives and well-perforating specialist competence
groups.role: Site coordinators; Adjacent-trade supervisors; Support personnel preparing for specialist instruction
groups.scopeConfirmation: Seismic acquisition may be nonexplosive. Construction blasting rules are bounded examples, not universal well-perforating law.

groups.title: Well-control and production-safety role competence
groups.role: Well-service support coordinators; Personnel preparing for role-specific well-control instruction; Supervisor/technical interface personnel
groups.scopeConfirmation: Drilling, fishing, plugging, mud engineering, logging and stimulation roles remain distinct. Nitrogen, radiation and explosives activate only for actual tools and duties.

groups.title: Pesticide handling and application task safety
groups.role: Pesticide job coordinators; Handlers preparing for approved product/equipment instruction; Maintenance and receiving personnel at pesticide interfaces
groups.scopeConfirmation: Agricultural WPS, structural pest control, industrial use and nonchemical grounds work have different applicability; SDS training alone is insufficient.

groups.title: Discipline-specific professional engineering and design authority
groups.role: Assigned design engineers; Design coordinators; Discipline technical reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Desk design is distinct from field execution. Marine/ice or pipeline engineering parent labels can include varied subscopes; resolve actual duties.

groups.title: Non-safety professional authorization, financial controls and privacy
groups.role: Actual contracted professional or technical duty must be established
groups.scopeConfirmation: A broad consultancy or office service does not establish a regulated professional act; determine actual scope before declaring a credential gap.

groups.title: Task-specific electrical, instrument and commissioning competence
groups.role: Electrical work planners; Instrument service coordinators; Assigned commissioning document reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: General electrical/instrument work is not automatically electric-power work under G11. IT installation and generator service must identify actual electrical exposure.

groups.title: Refrigerant and HVAC method qualification
groups.role: HVAC technicians learning service planning; Facility service coordinators; Vendor evidence reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Certification applies to defined refrigerant-service activities and equipment; do not assign it to desk HVAC designers or all facility workers.

groups.title: Aviation operating, maintenance and ground-role qualification
groups.role: Assigned aviation ground coordinators; Customer logistics personnel; Aviation service planners
groups.scopeConfirmation: Aircraft rental does not imply a supplied pilot; passengers, auditors, ground crew and aircrew retain different requirements.

groups.title: Method-specific NDT, inspection and technical certification authority
groups.role: NDT trainees in a bounded theory role; Inspection coordinators; Technical report reviewers
practicalAssessmentRequired: 10 CFR 34.43(b)(4), (c)(3), (f) — Radiographers and radiographer assistants using licensed material in covered NRC industrial-radiography operations: The licensee must provide the applicable hardware practical examination and maintain the required training/examination records. These are radiography-role duties, not requirements for every NDT method or an awareness-course learner. Source: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title10-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title10-vol1-sec34-43.pdf
groups.scopeConfirmation: Visual/ultrasonic/penetrant/magnetic/radiographic methods differ. Load testing and notified-body labels need exact equipment/method review.

groups.title: Instrument service, metrology and calibration methods
groups.role: Instrument service trainees; Calibration technicians in a theory module; Measurement result reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Calibration is not automatically atmosphere testing; electrical and process-connection duties activate only when actually performed.

groups.title: Welding, fabrication and pressure-code craft competence
groups.role: Welding and fabrication trainees in a theory module; Fabrication coordinators; Assigned quality reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Not all piping uses welding and not all fabrication is pressure-code work. Preserve those actual-method distinctions.

groups.title: Hazardous-material survey, abatement and exposure-control methods
groups.role: Hazardous-material task trainees in a theory role; Maintenance planners; Assigned exposure-control coordinators
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.132(f)(2), (g) — Employees using the eye/face, head, foot, hand or personal fall protection covered by paragraph (g): Before that work, demonstrate understanding of the PPE training and ability to use the PPE properly. This is not a separate independent certification requirement. Respirators and electrical protective equipment follow their own standards rather than paragraph (f). Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.132

29 CFR 1910.134(e), (f), (k)(1) — Required respirator users; tight-fitting facepieces require the applicable fit test: Complete the required medical evaluation before fit testing or use, the applicable fit test, and training that enables demonstration of the listed knowledge and respirator-use skills. These duties apply to the actual respirator assignment, not everyone taking awareness training. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.134

29 CFR 1926.1101(k)(9)(iii)-(v) — Workers performing the particular construction asbestos work classes covered by these provisions: Use the training specified for the actual work class, including its applicable hands-on component and required course duration. General asbestos awareness does not impose these abatement-training requirements on a worker who does not perform that work. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1101
groups.scopeConfirmation: Silica dust, asbestos, lead, refractory and coatings are separate substances/tasks. Source mentions of them are not proof each is present.

groups.title: Nitrogen, inert-atmosphere, cryogenic and catalyst specialist tasks
groups.role: Specialist gas/catalyst trainees in a theory role; Nitrogen service planners; Process-interface coordinators
groups.scopeConfirmation: Resolve desk nitrogen engineering versus field nitrogen service; catalyst and inert-entry work need their own actual substance and rescue assessment.

groups.title: Lifting and mobile-equipment role-specific practical competence
groups.role: Lifting and mobile-equipment trainees in a theory module; Lift coordinators; Equipment service planners
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.178(l)(2), (4), (6) — Operators of powered industrial trucks covered by this standard: Formal instruction, practical training and workplace performance evaluation are required before independent operation, with employer certification and applicable refresher/evaluation duties. A trainer/evaluator needs the knowledge, training and experience specified in (l)(2)(iii); an outside assessor is not universally required. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.178

29 CFR 1926.1427(a), (f) — Operators of construction cranes/equipment covered by Subpart CC, subject to the stated exceptions: Meet the applicable operator training/certification or licensing provisions and employer evaluation requirements for the equipment and assigned work. Do not apply this crane rule to every lifting worker or every piece of mobile equipment. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1427

29 CFR 1926.1428(a), (c)(5) — Construction crane signal persons covered by Subpart CC: Demonstrate the specified knowledge through an oral or written test and a practical test. The standard permits a qualified third-party evaluator or the employer's qualified evaluator, with the stated documentation and portability limits. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1428
groups.scopeConfirmation: Rental without operator does not include operation. Grader/roller operation is not a crane qualification, and a rigger is not automatically a lift engineer.

groups.title: Machine, trade, thermal-treatment and repair methods
groups.role: Machine/trade trainees in a theory module; Repair and treatment coordinators; Technical maintenance reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Mechanical repair, heat treatment, grounds machinery, printing and material treatment are retained as distinct method variants, not one universal operator qualification.

groups.title: Pressure testing, technical acceptance and specialist live-leak intervention
groups.role: Pressure-work trainees in a theory module; Test planners; Process/technical acceptance coordinators
groups.scopeConfirmation: Live-process leak sealing is not routine depressurized line opening. Preserve that specialist variant and actual system scope.

groups.title: Survey, seismic acquisition and field-method competence
groups.role: Survey/seismic trainees in a theory module; Field-data coordinators; Technical deliverable reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Seismic source may be nonexplosive. Survey labels do not automatically imply diving, drilling or aerial operation.

groups.title: Security, lawful conflict management and post-specific duties
groups.role: Assigned security-post trainees; Access coordinators; Security supervisors reviewing post readiness
groups.scopeConfirmation: Guarding differs from security-system installation. Actual jurisdiction and duties govern credentials.

groups.title: Facility support, water hygiene and biological task methods
groups.role: Facility-support trainees in a theory module; Water/hygiene program coordinators; Support-service planners
groups.scopeConfirmation: Hotel, property lease, warehouse or personal support is not automatically catering, clinical care or contaminated laundry. Water hygiene is not identical to bloodborne-pathogen training.

groups.title: IT/OT cybersecurity and safety-critical change assurance
groups.role: Assigned IT/OT technical trainees in a theory module; Change coordinators; Recovery validation reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Differentiate desk software/support, network installation and changes affecting operating safeguards.

groups.title: Subject-specific instructor and practical assessor capability
groups.role: Assigned subject instructors; Training designers; Practical-assessment coordinators
groups.scopeConfirmation: Training-system consultancy is not automatically course delivery; no provider can create its own legal accreditation by naming a course.

groups.title: Safety audit, incident investigation and evidence methods
groups.role: Assigned incident investigators; Safety auditors; Investigation team members; Corrective-action reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: An investigator is not automatically an emergency responder, electrical inspector or licensed professional.

groups.title: Waste characterization, environmental sampling and treatment methods
groups.role: Waste characterization coordinators; Assigned environmental samplers; Laboratory liaison personnel; Waste acceptance and shipment reviewers
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.120(e)(3), (e)(4), (q)(6) — Workers whose actual hazardous-waste or emergency-response duties fall within the cited provisions: Apply the training and supervised field-experience or response-role competence requirements specified for that actual assignment. Do not assign the hazardous-waste field-experience requirement to ordinary waste handling or awareness-only roles. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.120
groups.scopeConfirmation: Nonhazardous disposal, hazardous waste, emergency response and environmental desk advice must remain distinct. HAZWOPER is not inferred from the word waste.

groups.title: Hydroblasting, hydrovac and specialist cleaning methods
groups.role: Assigned specialist cleaning crew members; Hydrovac and vacuum-transfer task planners; Cleaning supervisors; Equipment preparation and customer handover personnel
groups.scopeConfirmation: Travel/standby billing is not evidence of active hydrovac excavation; pressure-washer rental does not imply a supplied hydroblaster.

groups.title: Construction, utility-location and excavation methods
groups.role: Construction task planners; Excavation crew members; Utility-interface coordinators; Plant-interface supervisors; Construction handover reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Pipeline/LNG construction does not automatically include commissioning or process operation; method-specific roles activate only when supplied.

groups.title: Confined-space entry and rescue practical roles
groups.role: Assigned confined-space entrants; Assigned attendants and entry supervisors; Space-program coordinators; Rescue-readiness reviewers
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.146(k)(2)(iv) — Employer-designated employees performing covered permit-space rescue: Practice the assigned permit-space rescues at least every 12 months using the specified actual or representative spaces, subject to the real-rescue exception. This is a rescue-team duty, not a practical test required of every awareness-course learner. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.146
groups.scopeConfirmation: The underlying installation trade also needs its own competence; an entry qualification is not a repair qualification.

groups.title: Fall protection, scaffold and rope-access practical roles
groups.role: Workers using an assigned height-access system; Scaffold users and task supervisors; Rope-access planning coordinators; Fall-system and rescue-readiness reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: A scaffold user, scaffold inspector, rope-access technician and fall-protection designer have different scopes.

groups.title: Clinical professional scope and medical deployment
groups.role: Medical deployment coordinators; Clinical service supervisors; Clinical credential and governance reviewers; Clinic administrators and occupational exposure coordinators
groups.scopeConfirmation: C08 first-aid assurance is not medical licensing; office medical administration is not clinical care.

groups.title: Host-task, staffing and logistics role instruction
groups.role: Supplied workers and host supervisors; Staffing-agency placement coordinators; Logistics and receiving coordinators; Employer competence and assignment reviewers
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.178(l)(2), (4), (6) — Operators of powered industrial trucks covered by this standard: Formal instruction, practical training and workplace performance evaluation are required before independent operation, with employer certification and applicable refresher/evaluation duties. A trainer/evaluator needs the knowledge, training and experience specified in (l)(2)(iii); an outside assessor is not universally required. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.178
groups.scopeConfirmation: Recruitment and project/logistics management are not direct evidence of hands-on execution; confirm each person’s duties.

groups.title: Research-method and experimental protocol competence
groups.role: Research method leads and project researchers; Computational data analysts; Laboratory and field research coordinators; Technical protocol and research-handover reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Geology, IT or petroleum R&D may be desk-only; do not infer a laboratory or field experiment from the research label.

groups.title: Pipeline operating, pigging and inline-inspection methods
groups.role: Pipeline field and control-room coordination personnel; Assigned pigging and inline-inspection support personnel; Tool/run planning specialists; Inspection data and operational handover reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Pipeline transportation is distinct from pipeline construction. Inline inspection is not automatically radiography.

groups.title: Asset-specific preparation, inspection and rental handoff
groups.role: Rental asset preparation and inspection personnel; Equipment dispatch and return coordinators; Customer handover supervisors; Asset condition and technical acceptance reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Rental without an operator is supply. Preserve this boundary for tanks, compressors, aircraft, lighting, power swivels and spill booms rather than assigning every operator credential to every rental.

groups.title: Unresolved service method, equipment or transport-mode scope
groups.role: Actual contracted professional or technical duty must be established
groups.scopeConfirmation: Retain explicit holds for generic inspection/testing, Lift work, nitrogen service, broad engineering parents and unspecified passenger mode.

serviceEvidence.sourceContext: Instrument testing/calibration is a broad supplier classification; it does not identify the instrument, measurement or work environment.
Load testing classification does not establish the asset, test type or energy involved.
Photogrammetry surveying does not establish aerial acquisition or a supplied aircraft operator.
Nitrogen Unit Engineering Services identifies engineering scope, not an established nitrogen operating method.
BPCL E. Hiring work > Hiring Equipments: Hiring of Tank / Pipeline is supply context and does not establish included operation.
Passenger Transport Services does not identify road, rail, marine or aviation mode.
BPCL inspection-services wording does not identify a technical inspection method.
BPCL H. Mechanical works > Installation/Maintenance of Equipment: original wording Lift work. It is not evidence of crane operation and does not conclusively establish elevator work.

serviceEvidence.serviceName: Process / Utilities / Piping / HVAC Engineering Services
serviceEvidence.sourceContext: Process / Utilities / Piping / HVAC Engineering Services is a broad engineering parent containing alternatives.
Non-destructive testing services includes multiple possible methods; radiography is not established by the parent label.

serviceEvidence.serviceName: Lease or Rental of Property or Building
serviceEvidence.sourceContext: Lease or Rental of Property or Building does not establish construction, maintenance or operational service.
Luboil Services is insufficient to distinguish supply, sampling, analysis, lubrication work or machinery intervention.
Pipeline Engineering Services does not itself establish construction, pigging or pipeline operating duties.
Navigation / Positioning Services does not establish marine, aviation, land-survey or desk-processing mode.
SEQual 91111500 Domestic and Personal Assistance includes laundering context; it does not automatically establish clinical laundry or occupational blood exposure.
Personnel / Training System Consultancy does not establish direct instruction in every technical trade.
Heat exchanger testing services does not identify pressure, leak, performance, NDT or another test method.

serviceEvidence.serviceName: Material Technology / Anti-Corrosion / Surface Protection Engineering Services
serviceEvidence.sourceContext: Material Technology / Anti-Corrosion / Surface Protection Engineering Services contains several engineering alternatives.
Permitting Services does not establish whether the vendor prepares administrative applications, supplies professional studies or issues site work permits.
SEQual 71151502 Hydrocarbon Measurement sits under Hydrocarbon Allocation Management and Consultancy; it does not establish hands-on meter maintenance.
Navigational Services does not establish the operating mode or whether operating personnel are supplied.

groups.title: Vehicle, combination, cargo and driver practical qualification
groups.role: Assigned drivers within confirmed vehicle scope; Transport dispatch and receiving coordinators; Vehicle/trailer readiness reviewers; Cargo and journey-planning supervisors
groups.scopeConfirmation: Rental self-drive, chauffeured service, carrier operation and office dispatch are different roles. Regulated hazardous cargo is separately classified under G01.

groups.title: Language, travel and media equipment task instruction
groups.role: Assigned technical interpreters and translators; Guides and travel coordinators; Ground photography and media-production personnel; Technical-content and site-access reviewers
groups.scopeConfirmation: Ground photography is not UAS operation; an interpreter does not acquire the technical trade authority of the people being interpreted.

groups.title: Industrial fire brigade and specialist emergency response
groups.role: Assigned industrial emergency-response coordinators; Brigade supervisors and readiness reviewers; Incident-command liaison personnel; Exercise planners and evaluators within confirmed scope
groups.scopeConfirmation: Fire-system maintenance does not make the technician a firefighter. Recognition/notification, defensive response and hazardous intervention have different roles.

groups.title: Fire/protection-system service and impairment methods

groups.scopeConfirmation: Maintain the distinction between servicing a protective system and performing fire brigade response.

extensions.name: H2S Monitoring & Safety Trailer
scopeNotes: H2S monitoring and safety-trailer work can involve separate detector-use, monitoring, gas-testing, respiratory-equipment, rescue and calibration duties.
Apply only the roles and tasks actually included in your service and assigned to each person.

roleMappings.role: Worker exposed to H2S who wears an assigned personal detector
roleMappings.trigger: Actual exposure and assigned detector use; teach only the relevant user functions.
roleMappings.rationale: Recognize the exposure, alarm response and escape boundaries, and understand the assigned detector's checks and limitations. Wearing a detector does not authorize clearance testing, service or rescue.

roleMappings.trigger: Actual setup, operation, checking or monitoring duties.
roleMappings.rationale: The technician must understand detector selection, bounded sampling/measurement, assurance checks, defects, positioning and alarm communication within the monitoring plan.

roleMappings.role: Designated gas tester or permit-atmosphere verifier
roleMappings.trigger: Only a formally assigned gas-testing or permit-verification duty.
roleMappings.rationale: C07 teaches endorsement assurance. Instrument- and task-specific practical assessment and employer/site authorization remain necessary; these courses do not grant gas-clearance authority.

roleMappings.role: Breathing-air equipment technician or assigned respirator user
roleMappings.trigger: Only actual respiratory-equipment duties or required respirator use; not every H2S worker.
roleMappings.rationale: Respirator selection, medical evaluation, fit testing where applicable, breathing-air quality and equipment-specific operation require the appropriate program and separately verified task capability.

Knowledge foundations support response planning; the rescue mode, equipment, team exercises, medical/first-aid competence and applicable response-level qualification must be separately assessed. No unprotected rescue entry is authorized.

roleMappings.trigger: Only calibration, maintenance or repair functions actually supplied.
roleMappings.rationale: Manufacturer- and model-specific service instruction, reference standards and release-to-service competence are not established by a user's bump-test knowledge.

residualRequirements.title: Worker exposed to H2S who wears an assigned personal detector
residualRequirements.role: Worker exposed to H2S who wears an assigned personal detector
residualRequirements.scopeConfirmation: Actual exposure and assigned detector use; teach only the relevant user functions.

residualRequirements.title: Gas-monitoring installation and monitoring technician
residualRequirements.scopeConfirmation: Actual setup, operation, checking or monitoring duties.

residualRequirements.scopeConfirmation: Only a formally assigned gas-testing or permit-verification duty.

practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.134(e), (f), (k)(1) — Required respirator users; tight-fitting facepieces require the applicable fit test: Complete the required medical evaluation before fit testing or use, the applicable fit test, and training that enables demonstration of the listed knowledge and respirator-use skills. These duties apply to the actual respirator assignment, not everyone taking awareness training. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.134
residualRequirements.scopeConfirmation: Only actual respiratory-equipment duties or required respirator use; not every H2S worker.

residualRequirements.title: Assigned H2S rescue/response team
practicalAssessmentRequired: 29 CFR 1910.146(k)(2)(iv) — Employer-designated employees performing covered permit-space rescue: Practice the assigned permit-space rescues at least every 12 months using the specified actual or representative spaces, subject to the real-rescue exception. This is a rescue-team duty, not a practical test required of every awareness-course learner. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.146

residualRequirements.title: Detector calibration/repair technician
residualRequirements.scopeConfirmation: Only calibration, maintenance or repair functions actually supplied.
